data.loadout_text:
# Built-in loadout: fix. Owner: workstream review-qa.
# One writer, the project's required checks, and a required review by a
# different model (up to three rounds). The reviewer numbers its findings
# F1, F2, ...; the writer answers every finding the host sends back with
# accept or reject and a reason, in an ADJUDICATIONS block, and the host
# records each answer (a finding left unanswered is "missing" and the run
# needs attention). A reviewer on the writer's model is warned about, not
# refused.
schema: axocoatl.loadout/1
id: fix
version: 1
name: Fix
description: >-
  One writer makes the change; the host runs the required checks on the exact
  final files and a reviewer on a different model must approve the result.
kind: fix
params:
  writer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the writer
  reviewer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the reviewer (use a different model than the writer)
agents:
  - id: writer
    role: writer
    model: { param: writer_model }
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    instructions: >-
      You own this change. Find the relevant code and tests, make the change,
      run the project's check command and fix failures, then compare your diff
      with the task. When the host sends you review findings, answer every
      finding in an ADJUDICATIONS block: a line ADJUDICATIONS, then a fenced
      JSON array with one object per finding, {"id": "F1", "decision":
      "accept" or "reject", "reason": "..."}. Reject only with a concrete
      reason (the code that shows the finding is wrong). Fix each finding you
      accept, run the checks again, and give your final answer. Leave no file
      you created only for testing or debugging (scratch scripts, test binaries
      such as `go test -c` output, build outputs, reports): delete them, then
      run the project's check command one last time before your final answer.
checks:
  - name: tests
    run: { detected: true }
    timeout: 3m
review:
  model: { param: reviewer_model }
  rounds: 3
  tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
  adjudicate: true
  instructions: >-
    Review the change against the task and against every contract and edge
    case the docs, comments and tests describe. Read the code the change
    touches, not only the diff. Number each finding F1, F2, ... at the start
    of its line, with file:line, what is wrong and what to change; report
    only defects, not style. Give the verdict line the host asks for,
    VERDICT: APPROVE or VERDICT: CHANGES. Change nothing.
budgets:
  agent: { activations: 4, invocations: 400, tokens: 4000000, cost_usd: 10 }
  reviewer: { activations: 3, invocations: 120, tokens: 1500000, cost_usd: 3 }
  wall_clock: 60m
prompt: |
  {task}
sandbox:
  network: egress
  workload: hardened
